Viv Richards, born in St John's, Antigua, in 1952, was one of the greatest batsmen in the history of cricket. He played for the West Indies from 1974 to 1991 and captained the side from 1984.

He batted without a helmet and with great aggression, and his team did not lose a Test series under his captaincy. He won the World Cups of 1975 and 1979 with the West Indies, then the strongest side in the world.

For many in the Caribbean and beyond, the success of that team under Richards and Clive Lloyd was a statement of pride after colonial rule. The cricket ground at North Sound in Antigua is named after him, and he is often linked with Vere Bird as a national hero.
